successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: Eastern Xia's land, conquered by Güyük in 1233

ledger.x: 1215: Puxian Wannu founds the Eastern Xia.
1217: 'He again named his kingdom Eastern Xia or Dongxia' (after Great Zhen in 1215); the Goryeo called it Dongzhen.
1217: 'established the capital around Yanji and called it Nanjing'.
1217: 'His domain extended north to Laoyeling Mountains, south to Hamgyongnamdo in modern-day North Korea.'
1233: 'Puxian Wannu was captured and killed in the same year'; he was beheaded after his capture and the Eastern Xia 'collapsed nearly immediately afterwards'.

wars.name: Jin expedition against Puxian Wannu
wars.outcome: 1214: the Jin sent Puxian Wannu to Liaodong, where he was defeated around Kaiyuan; in 1215 he rebelled and founded the Eastern Xia.

wars.name: Eastern Xia revolt against the Mongols
wars.outcome: 1217: Wannu killed the Mongolian resident commissioners; by 1218 he had submitted again and Mongol and Eastern Xia armies jointly invaded Goryeo.

wars.name: Eastern Xia revolt of 1222
wars.outcome: 1222: Wannu revolted again while Genghis Khan was in the west; the page gives no outcome.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Eastern Xia
wars.outcome: 1233: Güyük conquered the kingdom in a few months, captured Puxian Wannu and had him beheaded.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the shape is Manchuria with the Hamgyong-namdo limit named in 1217.
